scenes.tts: Graft a second notochord against the side of a chick neural tube. The neural cells beside it start to behave like floor plate. The tube gains a second bottom. So how does a cell in the wall know how far it sits from the bottom? The answer is a signal called Sonic hedgehog.
scenes.visual: Tube with notochord below; a second notochord slides in at the side and that wall turns floor plate; question marks along the wall; yellow signal rises.
scenes.narration: Graft a second notochord against the side of a chick neural tube. The neural cells beside it start to behave like floor plate. The tube gains a second bottom. So how does a cell in the wall know how far it sits from the bottom? The answer is a signal called Sonic hedgehog.

scenes.tts: The floor plate and the notochord both make Sonic hedgehog. It spreads up the wall and falls off with distance. A signal that spreads from a source and gives different instructions at different concentrations is called a morphogen. Cells low in the wall receive a lot. Cells high in the wall receive little.
scenes.visual: One wall as a column of cells; yellow dots rise; a concentration curve is drawn beside it and the cells shade by amount.
scenes.narration: The floor plate and the notochord both make Sonic hedgehog. It spreads up the wall and falls off with distance. A signal that spreads from a source and gives different instructions at different concentrations is called a morphogen. Cells low in the wall receive a lot. Cells high in the wall receive little.

scenes.tts: Each cell answers with transcription factors. Class one factors are repressed by Sonic hedgehog, so they are lost where the signal is high. Class two factors need the signal, so they appear where it is high. Pax seven is switched off by low levels, so it marks the dorsal half. N K X two point two needs high levels, and it sits next to the floor plate.
scenes.caption: Each cell answers with transcription factors. Class I factors are repressed by Sonic hedgehog, so they are lost where the signal is high. scenes.visual: Same column; a class I curve (Pax7) falls toward the signal, a class II curve (Nkx2.2) rises toward it; cells take the colour of the factor they carry.
scenes.narration: Each cell answers with transcription factors. Class I factors are repressed by Sonic hedgehog, so they are lost where the signal is high. scenes.tts: But cells read more than the level. Sonic hedgehog switches on its own receptor, Patched one, so cells grow less sensitive and signaling fades. A higher dose keeps signaling going longer. At a fixed dose, longer exposure gives progressively more ventral identities. In this model, a cell's identity tracks something like the total signaling it has received.

scenes.tts: A smooth slope should give a blur, yet the borders are sharp. Factors on either side of a border repress each other. Pax six and N K X two point two do this where the motor neuron domain meets the domain below. Two such factors form a switch with two stable states. A cell near the border falls to one side, and stays there.

scenes.tts: The result is five ventral stripes of progenitors. From top to bottom they are p zero, p one, p two, p M N and p three. They make V zero, V one and V two interneurons, motor neurons, and V three neurons. Keep this rule. A source makes a slope, cells read its level and its duration, and cross-repression sharpens it into domains.
